facts.title: SmartGen: Seamless Disaggregated LLM Inference with Selective KV Cache Transfer
facts.event_hint: SmartGen importance-aware selective KV cache transfer for disaggregated LLM inference
facts.problem: Prefill/decoding disaggregation requires moving large KV caches between nodes. On low-bandwidth rented cloud instances this transfer can saturate the RDMA link, stall decoding, and increase time-to-second-token, especially for long prompts.
facts.mechanism: SmartGen divides KV entries into universally important, context-dependent, and less-important classes. A profile-based proactive path pushes universally important entries during prefill; a parallel on-demand path fetches context-dependent entries during decoding while overlapping remote fetch with local KV loading; a speculative path transfers remaining entries during network idle periods. The design uses dynamic KV sparsity to reduce bytes on the transition path while retaining missing entries for accuracy.

evidence.claim: Compared with typical full KV-cache transfer, SmartGen reduces time-to-second-token by up to 4.3x while keeping subsequent decoding performance and accuracy comparable.
evidence.condition: Evaluated across Llama-3.1, Qwen3, Gemma-3, and Phi-4 with real-world workloads

evidence.claim: For 48K-token prompts on Alibaba Cloud L20 instances with a 25 Gbps RDMA network, KV transfer takes 6.5x longer than prefill computation.
evidence.condition: Llama and Qwen models; long-context prompt of 48K tokens; L20 GPUs; 25 Gbps RDMA

evidence.claim: The stage-transition KV-transfer stall can account for up to 42.2% of job completion time.
evidence.condition: Disaggregated inference under limited inter-node bandwidth

evidence.claim: The analysis testbed used three Alibaba Cloud prefill instances, each with two NVIDIA L20 GPUs, one decoding instance with one L20 GPU, and a 25 Gbps RDMA interface; KV caches were offloaded to host memory.
evidence.condition: Three prefill ecs.gn8is-2x.8xlarge instances and one decoding ecs.gn8is.4xlarge instance
evidence.source_locator: PDF page 3, Section 3 Analysis of KV Cache Transfer

evidence.claim: SmartGen addresses two implementation challenges: selecting important KV entries before decoding queries are available and fetching missing entries without putting a network round trip on every attention layer's critical path.
evidence.condition: Selective KV transfer in prefill/decode-disaggregated serving

facts.evaluation_context: The paper integrates SmartGen with sparse-attention algorithms and evaluates Llama-3.1, Qwen3, Gemma-3, and Phi-4 over multiple real-world workloads. The motivating transfer analysis uses Alibaba Cloud instances with L20 GPUs, host-memory KV offload, and 25 Gbps RDMA; it assumes a 75% prefix-cache hit ratio for that analysis.
facts.limitations: The reported results are tied to the evaluated model families, sparse-attention integrations, workloads, and Alibaba Cloud L20/25 Gbps setup; the excerpt does not establish behavior on faster fabrics, other GPU/network combinations, or a broad accuracy envelope across sequence lengths. Selective transfer also depends on the quality of profile-based importance prediction and still requires on-demand remote fetches for context-dependent entries. The need for speculative completion and remote accesses implies residual bandwidth and latency sensitivity (inference).
facts.project_relevance: For TPN/KV-network scheduling, this is a concrete case where network policy can be driven by inference phase and KV-entry importance: proactively reserve bandwidth for predicted-important entries, overlap on-demand fetches with local work, and use idle capacity for speculative completion. It suggests evaluating TTST/TTFT and tail latency alongside transfer volume, while separating gains from sparse attention itself from gains attributable to network scheduling (inference).
